correctness.rationale: Independently rebuilt P4 square P5 as a 20-vertex 31-edge graph and all 120,465 matching faces, matching every cardinality coefficient [1,31,395,2696,10769,25835,36771,29580,12181,2111,95]. Independently followed the declared stagewise element matching (60,205 pairs), topologically checked all 120,465 augmented Hasse vertices, and recomputed oriented integral Morse boundaries: critical 1 zero-cell,5 five-cells,47 six-cells,1 seven-cell; the 5x47 D6 has 197 zero,23 negative-unit,15 positive-unit entries and determinant -1 on columns 0,1,2,15,19, while D7 has five stated ±1 entries, gcd1, and D6D7=0. In dimensions 5 and 6 homotopy classes of attaching maps to same-dimensional sphere wedges are determined by integer degrees; unimodular and primitive cancellations yield one point and 41 six-spheres. No claim extrapolates to all grids.

evidence: Matsushita full PDF introduction and theorem concern 2-by-n strips and generalized Delta_n^m; Braun–Hough PDF likewise concerns two-row narrow grid families. Neither states all-width rectangular grid homotopy.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A width-two complete classification cannot immediately deduce 4x5 homotopy; general topological matching-complex results give bounds, not the precise primitive integral attachments in this case.

value.rationale: The 4-by-5 path product is a canonical next larger two-dimensional grid, not an arbitrary induced graph, and its exact integral homotopy wedge detects more than matching-polynomial or Euler data. Complete primitive integer attaching information is a useful benchmark for grid matching-complex recurrences and torsion questions even absent a closed family formula.

limitations: Single nonperiodic P4-by-P5 matching complex; exact finite computation proves no rectangle-family theorem or natural equivariant decomposition.
